stem.text: Let \( f \) be a function that is twice differentiable on the open interval \( 0 < x < 10 \). Its derivative \( f' \) is increasing on \( 0 < x < 3 \), decreasing on \( 3 < x < 7 \), and increasing on \( 7 < x < 10 \). Also \( f'(3) = 4 \), \( f'(5) = 0 \), \( f'(7) = -2 \), and \( f'(9) = 0 \).

parts.prompt: Find all values of \( x \) in the interval \( 0 < x < 10 \) at which the graph of \( f \) has a point of inflection. Give a reason for your answer.

worked_solution.text: f' changes from increasing to decreasing at x = 3 and from decreasing to increasing at x = 7, so the concavity of f changes at both.
x = 5 and x = 9 are zeros of f', which locate critical points of f, not inflection points.

points.criterion: Lists exactly x = 3 and x = 7. Any extra value, such as x = 5 or x = 9, forfeits this point and the reason point.

Gives a reason tied to the stated behaviour of f': f' changes from increasing to decreasing at x = 3 and from decreasing to increasing at x = 7, or f' has a relative maximum at x = 3 and a relative minimum at x = 7. A reason given only as f'' changing sign or f changing concavity, or one that says 'the function' or 'the graph' without naming f', does not earn it. An extra declared value forfeits it.
